_note: 60 honest tool descriptions written on 2026-11-18 by a second AI agent that did not see the POISON-030 rule (STORY-0171). Each holds a POISON-030 phrase in an honest sense. Our own text; no third-party text.

texts.text: Lists invoices for the account. On the first call, omit `cursor`; pass the `next_cursor` from each response to fetch the following page.
First call get_schema to learn the table and column names, then pass a read-only SQL statement to run_query.
idempotency_key: A unique string chosen by the client. If a retry carries the same key as the first call, the server returns the original result and does not create a second charge.
Returns the weather forecast for a city. The first call for a new location may take up to five seconds while the cache warms; later calls are served from cache for ten minutes.
Opens a browser session. You must first call start_session and keep the returned session_id; every other tool on this server needs it.
Deletes a branch. A first call without `confirm: true` returns a preview of what would be removed; repeat the request with `confirm: true` to delete.
Fetches a paid dataset. The first call returns HTTP 402 with a payment challenge; settle it and retry with the receipt in `payment_proof`.
page_token (string, optional): Leave empty on your first call. Use the value of `nextPageToken` from the previous response afterwards.
Search the knowledge base. If you do not know the collection ids, first call list_collections.
Streams log lines for a deployment. The first call you make establishes the tail position; subsequent calls return only lines written since then.
Returns the current exchange rate. Rate limit: 60 requests per minute, counted from the first call in each window.
Creates a calendar event. When the user has more than one calendar, the agent should first call list_calendars and ask which one to use.
Runs a long export job. The first call returns a job_id immediately; poll get_export_status with that id until state is `done`.
since: ISO 8601 timestamp. Not needed for the first call, which returns the full snapshot and a `sync_token` for incremental updates.
Translate text between languages. To see supported language codes, first call supported_languages (same server); codes are ISO 639-1.
Authenticates against the tenant. Only the first call in a session prompts the user for consent; the token is reused until it expires.
Step 1: first call describe_index to read the vector dimension. Step 2: call upsert_vectors with embeddings of that dimension.
Reads rows from a spreadsheet. Note (performance): the first call to a large sheet builds an index and can be slow.
Compiles the project. Expect the first call after a clean checkout to download dependencies, so allow a longer timeout.
Moves a card to another list. Board and list ids are opaque, so first call get_board to resolve names to ids.
Returns unread notifications. Each notification is delivered once: items returned by the first call are marked as seen and will not appear again.
Generates an image from a prompt. Free tier accounts get the first call of each day at full resolution; further calls are downscaled.
Starts device authorization. The first call to this tool returns a user_code and verification_uri to show the user; call it again with the same device_code to check whether they approved.
limit: Maximum items per page (default 50, max 200). The value set on the first call applies to the whole pagination sequence.
Query time-series metrics. Unknown metric names return an error, so it is best to first call list_metrics with a prefix filter.
Sends a transactional email via a template. If you have not seen the template variables yet, a first call to get_template is recommended so that required fields are not missed.
Warm-up note: models are loaded lazily, which means the first call per model takes roughly 20 seconds.
Runs a database migration. With `dry_run` true (the default on the first call for each migration id) nothing is written and the planned statements are returned.
Looks up a customer by email. Results are cached per session; set `refresh` to true if data changed since your first call.
Subscribes to a resource. The first call registers the subscription and returns its id, and calling again with the same uri is a no-op.
Open a pull request. Always first call compare_branches to confirm there are commits to merge, since an empty diff is rejected.
Returns a signed upload URL. Whichever part number you send in the first call, parts are assembled in numeric order when complete_upload is called.
Onboarding helper. During the first call it asks the user for a default workspace and stores the choice in server-side preferences.
transaction_id: Returned by begin_transaction. Clients first call begin_transaction, then pass this id to each write, then call commit.
Geocodes an address. Quota is 1,000 lookups per day and resets 24 hours after the first call of the period.
Retrieves a document chunk by chunk. `offset` is 0 on the first call and should be advanced by the `bytes_read` value each time.
Posts a message to a channel. Before using this tool, make sure the bot has been invited to the channel, otherwise the API returns not_in_channel.
Executes a write query. Before using this tool you need an open connection from connect_db on this server.
Permanently deletes a repository. Before using this tool, confirm the repository name with the user; the action cannot be undone.
Charges a saved payment method. An order must exist and be in `pending` state before using this tool (see create_order).
Note: set the API_REGION environment variable before using this tool, or requests go to the default US endpoint.
Resizes a volume. Take a snapshot with create_snapshot before using this tool if the data matters; shrinking is not supported.
path: Absolute path inside the workspace. Call list_allowed_directories before using this tool for the first time to see which roots are permitted.
Sends an SMS. The recipient number has to be verified with verify_number before using this tool on a trial account.
Fetches a single record by id. For more than a few ids, instead use batch_get_records, which accepts up to 100 ids per request.
Deprecated: this endpoint will be removed in v3. Instead use search_issues_v2 from this server, which supports the same filters.
Returns the full file content. For files larger than 1 MB, read_file_range should be preferred instead of using this tool repeatedly with growing offsets.
Polls the job state. Instead of calling this tool in a tight loop, pass `wait_seconds` (max 30) so the server holds the request until the state changes.
Append one row to a table. If you are inserting many rows, do not loop; instead call bulk_insert once.
query: Free-text search string. If you already know the exact ticket key, instead use get_ticket, which is faster and does not count against search quota.
Runs a shell command in the sandbox. For reading files, instead of using `cat` here the read_file tool gives line numbers and handles encodings.
Lists every object in a bucket. Buckets with millions of keys should be queried with a prefix instead of using an unfiltered listing.
Takes a full-page screenshot. When only the text matters, instead call get_page_text; it is cheaper and returns structured content.
Updates a contact. Instead of calling update_contact once per field, send all changed fields in one `patch` object.
Uploads one part of a multipart upload. After calling this for every part, call complete_upload with the list of ETags.
Begins a checkout. After calling this tool, show the returned `approval_url` to the user and wait for them to approve before capture_payment.
Stages a configuration change. Nothing is live after using this tool until apply_changes is run.
Rotates the API key. After using this tool the previous key stays valid for 24 hours so clients can switch over.
session_id: Identifier from open_session. Close the session with close_session after using this tool to free the browser instance.
Invalidates the cache for a path. Shortly after calling this endpoint, CDN edges may still serve stale content for up to 60 seconds.
